nodes.label: CyberAlchemy Language Project
nodes.plain_language: The durable project that keeps language goals, owners, evidence, practices, mappings, and open questions connected.
nodes.claim: The Language Runtime is one proposed realization inside the Language Project, not the Project itself.
nodes.scope: Projection of the existing private Language Project identity.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the project folder, one runtime, one session, or authority to implement every language goal.

nodes.label: Ubiquitous Language First-Example Goal
nodes.plain_language: Create one reviewable bounded language example and show how its meaning can travel without being silently redefined.
nodes.claim: The first runtime experiment should exercise this Goal without treating package generation as Goal achievement.
nodes.scope: Projection of the active, not-proved Language Project Goal.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus Governance bounded-context language owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not achieved because an ontology, CLI, session, or candidate artifact exists.
open_questions: Which runtime evidence will support the partial Define-integration condition?

nodes.label: CyberAlchemy Governance Ubiquitous Language
nodes.plain_language: The first bounded language asset the runtime should load and evolve through reviewable questions.
nodes.claim: The first experiment uses this candidate Language as input and must preserve its context, owners, meanings, and unresolved choices.
nodes.scope: Governance bounded context only.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy Governance bounded-context language owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the universal CyberAlchemy language, canonical definition store, glossary, ontology, or runtime state.

nodes.label: Governance Policy Language-Resolution Exercise
nodes.plain_language: The exact current in-progress example that maps Governance Policy, Rule Review Recommendation, and Rule Review Action while preserving the recommendation's unresolved identity question.
nodes.claim: The first runtime experiment uses this exact example as its semantic fixture and must not silently complete, broaden, or redefine it.
nodes.scope: Exact projection of cyberAlchemy-v2/language/examples/governance-policy-resolution.json at its registered source digest.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy Governance owner with definitions-governance review
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the whole Governance Ubiquitous Language, an accepted DomainSpec classification, a completed experiment, or canonical definitions.
open_questions: Does Rule Review Recommendation need designated identity and lifecycle, or is immutable equality-by-fields sufficient?

nodes.label: Ubiquitous Language Practice
nodes.plain_language: The recurring practice for discovering, negotiating, checking, and evolving one bounded language.
nodes.claim: Runtime transitions should support this practice without turning it into executable authority or the Language itself.
nodes.scope: Projection of the existing candidate Discipline.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 discipline-governance owner plus bounded-context language owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a Language, definition owner, promotion route, Runtime Contract, or implementation workflow.
open_questions: Which practice steps belong in the first runtime slice?

nodes.label: Define Shared Meaning
nodes.plain_language: Find the concepts required by a goal, recover relevant evidence, ask what is missing, and keep each concept resolved or visibly open.
nodes.claim: The Language Runtime is intended to provide one interactive realization of this capability for bounded language work.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central CyberAlchemy product capability and Define-owned product meaning.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Define product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not canonical definition promotion, Design approval, implementation authority, or proof that an interactive runtime exists.

nodes.label: Resolve Bounded Language Context
nodes.plain_language: Prepare the exact language a person or agent may safely use for one bounded context and intended use.
nodes.claim: The capability joins source-digest-bound meanings, realizations, relationship vocabulary, authority limits, owners, evidence, conflicts, and blocked uses without deciding unresolved language.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central product capability into the Language product bridge; no request schema, resolver runtime, or implementation is selected.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus bounded-context language owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a canonical definition source, implicit semantic inference, DomainSpec type selector, authority resolver, or implemented runtime.
open_questions: Which accepted JSON request and freshness contract should produce the view?

nodes.label: Language Context View
nodes.plain_language: A bounded, read-only view of the language usable for one context, intended use, and exact source epoch.
nodes.claim: The view preserves its language, context, intended use, exact sources and digests, usable bindings, unresolved conflicts, blocked uses, owners, and freshness for the consuming Define work.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central product output; exact JSON shape, cache, transport, and production runtime remain unresolved.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus consuming capability owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a copied canonical registry, accepted Definition Pack, mutable Session State, authority envelope, selected open realization, or proof of correct interpretation.
open_questions: What minimum closed JSON view remains deterministic and useful to an agent?

nodes.label: Definition Pack
nodes.plain_language: A structured candidate set of concept decisions, evidence, owners, relationships, visible open questions, and the exact bounded language consulted by Define.
nodes.claim: The runtime may emit one Definition Pack candidate only from an explicitly reviewed Session State revision while preserving every unresolved output-affecting concept and the Language Context View identity, digest, source epoch, and applied binding references.
nodes.scope: First experiment output candidate; exact carrier contracts and acceptance remain owned by the CyberAlchemy v2 Define owners and the bounded-context meaning owner.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Define product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a canonical registry, accepted input, approved Design, executable plan, or complete human intent.
open_questions: Which exact closed JSON carrier will the first experiment compare?

nodes.label: Resolve Or Expose Every Required Concept
nodes.plain_language: Every required concept has a supported disposition or remains a visible open question.
nodes.claim: The runtime must not silently drop required concepts while advancing or emitting artifacts.
nodes.scope: Product meaning of Define coverage.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Define product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not proof that open-ended human intent is complete.
open_questions: Which open questions block emission and which may travel as residue?

nodes.label: Resolve Context Progressively And Expose Insufficiency
nodes.plain_language: Use supplied and provenance-marked context progressively, then ask for more when it remains insufficient or indeterminate.
nodes.claim: The runtime must preserve where context came from and never turn inferred context into a user answer.
nodes.scope: One bounded Language or Define session.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not permission to infer private human state, treat inferred material as an answer, or bypass unresolved context.
open_questions: Which source and retention boundaries will the first runtime enforce?

nodes.label: Apply Bounded Language Or Expose The Gap
nodes.plain_language: Define applies exact usable language bindings and keeps missing, stale, conflicting, ambiguous, or owner-unresolved language visible.
nodes.claim: Every applied language meaning remains traceable to the consulted Language Context View and source digest; Define cannot invent equivalence, silently choose an open realization, or drop owner and blocked-use information.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central Define Language-application rule into this business-system bridge.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Define product owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not permission to infer missing meaning, promote a definition, choose an unresolved DomainSpec type, or claim correct agent interpretation.
open_questions: Which Definition Pack binding proves which view and bindings were applied?

nodes.label: Language Question
nodes.plain_language: One visible question about meaning, evidence, conflict, scope, ownership, or a required concept disposition.
nodes.claim: A Language Question remains identifiable across interfaces until explicitly answered, deferred, withdrawn, or superseded.
nodes.scope: Local candidate business meaning for the Language Project runtime bridge.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus bounded-context meaning owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a system record, interface rendering, Answer, owner decision, or mandatory human gate.
open_questions: Should Language Question become a promoted Language Project definition after the first experiment?

nodes.label: Language Answer
nodes.plain_language: One explicit response to a Language Question, preserved with its speaker and context.
nodes.claim: A Language Answer can inform session state without becoming owner acceptance, canonical meaning, or permission to act.
nodes.scope: Local candidate business meaning for the Language Project runtime bridge.

source_refs.selector: a user answer changes the session state

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus named response owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not inferred context, machine suggestion, system record, owner decision, definition promotion, or execution authority.
open_questions: Which response kinds need separate business meanings after the first experiment?

nodes.label: Reviewable Next Step
nodes.plain_language: The person can see what needs attention, why it follows, what remains open, and which action is allowed or blocked.
nodes.claim: The Language Runtime should make the next language question or artifact reviewable rather than merely generating output.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central CyberAlchemy product outcome.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not measured usability, correct recommendation, owner acceptance, or permission to execute.

nodes.label: Work Continuity
nodes.plain_language: The same work can continue after interruption without reconstructing its objective, active question, evidence, or unresolved residue from memory.
nodes.claim: Persistent Language Session State is intended to support this outcome, but persistence alone cannot prove it.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central CyberAlchemy product outcome.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not file persistence alone, successful handoff, measured burden reduction, or runtime correctness.

nodes.label: Keep Human Choice Visible
nodes.plain_language: The interface distinguishes suggestions, user responses, and owner decisions instead of presenting them as one action.
nodes.claim: The runtime must preserve these boundaries in state, transitions, and views.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central CyberAlchemy product rule.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a requirement for a human gate at every step and not proof that the interface preserves agency.

nodes.label: Keep Evidence And Owner Visible
nodes.plain_language: Questions, answers, concept dispositions, and candidate artifacts retain the evidence and owner routes that give them meaning.
nodes.claim: The runtime must not hide provenance or infer ownership from interface position.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central CyberAlchemy product rule.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Evidence, participation, ownership, recommendation, and authority remain distinct.

nodes.label: Dynamic Human-Machine Work Fit
nodes.plain_language: Show the right governed question and evidence at a useful depth and pace for the person's explicit context and current work.
nodes.claim: CLI and chat may vary presentation depth without changing question meaning, identity, ownership, or evidence.
nodes.scope: Projection of the central first-order product principle.

source_refs.selector: change explanation depth and interaction speed

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not inferred attention, surveillance, measured usability, or permission to alter semantic content for convenience.
open_questions: Which ergonomic qualities will the first experiment observe without inferring private state?

nodes.label: Review Before Candidate Emission
nodes.plain_language: A draft preview may be shown before review, but a candidate may be materialized only after review of the exact Session State revision, state digest, and preview digest, with every unresolved output-affecting concept still visible.
nodes.claim: Exact-preview review is a precondition for candidate materialization but is not owner acceptance, definition promotion, or publication authority; any output-affecting change invalidates it.
nodes.scope: Candidate product rule for the first Language Runtime experiment and Definition Pack candidate.

source_refs.selector: Review the whole set before handoff

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Define output owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an accepted Definition Pack, canonical definition, owner decision, Design approval, or execution authority.
open_questions: Which digest binds review to the exact Session State revision and candidate preview?

nodes.label: Language Runtime
nodes.plain_language: A proposed local process that coordinates one resumable language session and its reviewable candidate outputs.
nodes.claim: The smallest runtime should coordinate state, questions, CLI and chat views, transitions, and candidate emission without owning semantic promotion.
nodes.scope: Candidate design for one local, single-process Language/Define vertical slice.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Runtime owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the Language Project, Define meaning, accepted Runtime Contract, running process, or proof of usability or correctness.
open_questions: Should the first executable surface belong to CyberAlchemy v2 or a private implementation project?

nodes.label: Resumable Language Session Kernel
nodes.plain_language: The smallest proposed runtime boundary that applies one explicit command to validated session state, produces the next state and Question View, and restores that work after restart.
nodes.claim: The first proof should close deterministic transition and single-writer restart continuity before CLI presentation, chat transport, or artifact emission are added.
nodes.scope: Candidate Layer 0 boundary: pure transition plus one atomic local JSON Session Store.

source_refs.selector: a restart restores the visible state
same question has one stable identity in CLI and chat

nodes.plain_language: A proposed closed JSON agreement for the first runtime boundary, inputs, outputs, invariants, failures, validation, owner route, and claim ceiling.
nodes.claim: The candidate may specify the kernel but cannot accept itself, authorize implementation, or prove conformance.

nodes.plain_language: The proposed pre-code semantic frame for testing whether one runtime slice preserves the bounded Governance Policy exercise through interruption and Definition Pack candidate emission.
nodes.claim: The frame names frozen inputs, invariants, comparator, measures, stop rules, and claim ceiling; a separate Experiment record, admitted run, and findings are still required.
nodes.scope: Candidate evidence-design artifact for the first Governance Ubiquitous Language runtime experiment.

source_refs.selector: Designed, Run, And Concluded Are Different

nodes.label: Language Session
nodes.plain_language: The identity-bearing boundary for one resumable language interview, its objective, active state, and lifecycle.
nodes.claim: One Language Session coordinates changing state and records without becoming the Language Project or the Language it discusses.
nodes.scope: Candidate system aggregate for one bounded runtime interaction.
nodes.owner_route: candidate CyberAlchemy v2 Language Runtime owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the runtime component, persisted state value, Language Project, conversation transcript, or owner decision lifecycle.

nodes.label: Language Session State
nodes.plain_language: One durable record of the objective, active question, answers, evidence, dispositions, unresolved work, and next allowed or blocked action.
nodes.claim: A restart should restore the same visible work state instead of treating interruption as completion.

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Runtime owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not canonical language state, user identity, owner acceptance, execution authority, or a transcript of private inferred state.

nodes.label: Language Session Store
nodes.plain_language: The first persistence boundary saves one complete validated JSON Session State and rejects a stale, corrupt, truncated, or invalid candidate replacement while retaining the prior valid bytes under the one-writer protocol.
nodes.claim: The first runtime uses one local process and one writer with whole-snapshot replacement; crash or power-loss durability requires separate platform evidence.
nodes.scope: Candidate atomic single-writer local JSON store; no crash-durability, database, socket, event-sourcing, or concurrent-writer claim.

source_refs.selector: a restart restores the visible state
